::: {#sol-log-loss-slope}

Write $\obsloss{i}$ for image $i$'s [log loss](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html#def-log-loss),
$\obsloss{i} = -\outvar_i \log \hprob_i - (1 - \outvar_i) \log (1 - \hprob_i)$.
Its derivative with respect to $\hprob_i$ is

$$
\derivf{\obsloss{i}}{\hprob_i} = -\frac{\outvar_i}{\hprob_i} + \frac{1 - \outvar_i}{1 - \hprob_i}.
$$

Since $\hprob_i = \sigmoidf{\predvar_i - \param}$,
the chain rule and the derivative of the logistic function give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\derivf{\hprob_i}{\param}
&= \sigmoid'(\predvar_i - \param) \cdot \derivf{}{\param} (\predvar_i - \param) \\
&= \hprob_i (1 - \hprob_i) \cdot (-1) \\
&= -\hprob_i (1 - \hprob_i).
\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the two,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\derivf{\obsloss{i}}{\param}
&= \derivf{\obsloss{i}}{\hprob_i} \cdot \derivf{\hprob_i}{\param} \\
&= \paren{-\frac{\outvar_i}{\hprob_i} + \frac{1 - \outvar_i}{1 - \hprob_i}} \cdot \paren{-\hprob_i (1 - \hprob_i)} \\
&= \outvar_i (1 - \hprob_i) - (1 - \outvar_i) \hprob_i \\
&= \outvar_i - \outvar_i \hprob_i - \hprob_i + \outvar_i \hprob_i \\
&= \outvar_i - \hprob_i.
\end{aligned}
$$

$\hR$ is the mean of the $\obsloss{i}$, so its derivative is the mean of theirs:

$$
\derivf{\hR}{\param} = \frac{1}{\nobs} \sumin (\outvar_i - \hprob_i).
$$

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
x_np, y_np = ink_01.numpy(), is_one.numpy()
p_np = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(x_np - 5)))
slope_by_hand = np.mean(y_np - p_np)
print(slope_by_hand)
```

At $\param = 5$ the slope is `r sprintf("%.4f", py$slope_by_hand)`.
It is negative, so raising the cutoff from 5 lowers the log loss.

:::
